issues.description: The problem statement and UML require a constructor SealSaloon(String) (a saloon name parameter), but both the provided template usage (Main) and the reference solution implement and use a no-argument constructor SealSaloon(). This constructor-parameter mismatch will confuse students about which constructor signature to implement and may cause tests or the provided Main to fail if they follow the problem text verbatim.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the constructor requirement consistent across artifacts. Either (A) update the problem statement/UML to require a no-argument SealSaloon() constructor (matching the template Main and solution), or (B) change the template Main and the solution to call and provide a public SealSaloon(String name) constructor. To maximize compatibility for students, implement a constructor SealSaloon(String name) and also keep or add a no-arg constructor (or provide an overloaded constructor) so both usages are supported.

issues.description: The problem statement explicitly specifies a SealSaloon constructor that accepts a String parameter (the saloon name) but both the provided template usage and the reference solution implement a no-argument constructor. This mismatch between the required constructor signature in the problem description and the code in template/solution can confuse students about the expected API and how to wire the saloon identity into their implementation.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the constructor signature consistent across artifacts. Either (A) update the template and solution to provide a constructor SealSaloon(String name) that initializes the object (and keep any existing no-arg constructor only as an overload), and update Main usage accordingly; or (B) update the problem statement to require a no-argument constructor. Prefer (A) if the saloon name is semantically important: add a private final String name field, a public SealSaloon(String name) constructor that sets it, and keep or overload a no-arg constructor only if needed for backward compatibility.
